thread.title: Stocks Inch Up At Open: Amazon Target Raised, Fed Minutes Loom

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stocks Inch Up At Open: Amazon Target Raised, Fed Minutes Loom
text:
Stocks opened to narrow gains Wednesday as McDonald's ( MCD ) and Apple ( AAPL ) led the Dow and investors looked toward this afternoon's release of minutes from the Federal Reserve.
X The Nasdaq Composite popped 0.5% at the starting bell as Apple jumped 0.8% and all four FANG stock tech leaders gained ground.
The Dow   added 0.2%. The S&P 500 posted a 0.3% gain — Advance Auto Parts ( AAP ) spiked 9% to top the index, after reporting a big revenue and earnings beat in its fourth quarter. Other auto parts names also rallied , with AutoZone ( AZO ) rising more than 3% and O'Reilly Auto ( ORLY ) up more than 1%.
In economic news , researcher Markit releases its preliminary composite purchasing managers index for February at 9:45 a.m. ET. January existing home sales are expected from the National Association of Realtors at 10 a.m. ET. At 2 p.m. ET, minutes from the Federal Open Market Committee's January meeting will be released. The notes will be scoured for signs as to whether the Fed may be considering upping its rate hike outlook to four increases for this year. There is also some speculation regarding a temporary increase of the inflation target, to more than 2%.
The dollar was rising ahead of the Fed minutes, placing some pressure on commodities. U.S. benchmark oil traded down 0.7%, copper was down 0.5%.
Walmart's Target Lowered, Amazon's Hiked; HealthEquity, PagSeguro Rising McDonald's jumped 1.1% to the head of the Dow in early trade. Walmart ( WMT ) added 0.2%% in early action, as Raymond James powered its price target on the stock to 110 from 113 after its massive 10% sell-off following its Q4 report on Tuesday. The loss erased all of the stock's gains for 2018, leaving shares at their lowest level since the company reported its third-quarter results on Nov. 16.
Amazon.com ( AMZN ) rose 1.1% after MKM Partners hoisted the stock's price target to 1750, up from 1,350. On Tuesday, the stock ran against the market, rising 1.4% in firm trade. The move continued the stock's rebound from support at the 10-week moving average, pushing shares almost to the 20% profit-taking level, following a flat base breakout in January.

Earnings news drove some of the morning's harshest declines, with Tile Shops ( TTS ) down 29% and U.S. Silica Holdings ( SCLA ) tumbling nearly 13%.
Cardtronics ( CATM ) fell 5% after reporting a solid fourth-quarter sales and earnings beat, but guiding full-year revenue and earnings below expectations. The stock had climbed 56% from a November low, but met stiff resistance at its 10-week moving average at the start of February.
IBD 50 and Leaderboard stock HealthEquity ( HQY ) grabbed an early 1.1% gain. The medical financial services outfit is just beyond buy range above a 52.53 buy point in a cup-with-handle base.
Brazilian issue PagSeguro Digital ( PAGS ) dipped 1% at the open. Also an IBD 50 and Leaderboard name, shares rose more than 4% on Tuesday following a breakout from an IPO base Friday. The stock ended Tuesday up 47% from its Jan. 24 IPO price.
